info.name: Food Track API
info.description: FoodTrack's own .NET API (all endpoints live in api/src/FoodTrack.Api/Endpoints). Requires an environment with `baseUrl` and `idToken` set -- see food-track-api.postman_environment.json. Every request except the two Health checks requires a valid Firebase ID token in `idToken`; there is no client sign-in flow yet (no mobile app), so mint one another way (e.g. a temporary Firebase Auth test page, or ask for a throwaway custom-token exchange) and paste it into the environment.

request.description: No auth required. Confirms the API process is up.
Requires auth -- it performs a real Firestore read, unlike the plain /health check. Confirms the Firebase Admin SDK credentials and project connectivity are working.
Returns 404 until the caller has upserted a profile at least once.

Full replace (create-or-update). gender: Male|Female|TransMale|TransFemale|Nonbinary|Other. activityLevel: Sedentary|Light|Moderate|Active|VeryActive. targetWeightKilograms, dailyWaterTargetMilliliters, dailyProteinTargetGrams, dailyCarbsTargetGrams and dailyFatTargetGrams are all optional goals (omit or null) -- only dailyCalorieTarget and desiredCalorieDeficit are required.

Permanently deletes the caller's meals, water and weight entries, custom foods, profile and Firebase sign-in account, then returns 204. Safe to repeat if a previous attempt failed partway. Irreversible -- only run it with a test account's token.

query.description: The caller's UTC offset in minutes (e.g. -180 for Brasilia). Days are grouped by the caller's own calendar day instead of UTC. Optional, defaults to 0.

request.description: LoggedAt is set to the current server time and returned in the response; there is no date field on create.
LoggedAt is preserved from the original entry, not reset to the edit time.

query.description: The caller's UTC offset in minutes (e.g. -180 for Brasilia). Days are grouped by the caller's own calendar day instead of UTC. Optional, defaults to 0.

request.description: Cache-first: searches Firestore by name prefix, falls back to TACO (generic/prepared Brazilian foods) and Open Food Facts (Brazilian branded products) on a miss and caches every result. First call for a new query is slower (external API round trips); repeat calls are cache hits. q must be at least 3 characters (400 otherwise) -- this guards the external APIs from a search-as-you-type client firing one request per keystroke. Both sources are Portuguese, so search in Portuguese (e.g. "peito de frango").
id here is FoodTrack's own FoodId (from a Search Foods result), not the external source's own id (TACO's numeric id or Open Food Facts' barcode).

Creates a personal food (FoodSource.Custom). Nutrition is per 100 of baseUnitType: Gram (a food) or Milliliter (a drink); left out, as here, it is Gram. Only visible to the authenticated user who created it -- it never shows up in another user's Search Foods results.
Same endpoint as Create Custom Food, for a drink: nutrition per 100 ml, and meal items for it are logged in Milliliter. Any baseUnitType other than Gram or Milliliter is a 400.
The authenticated user's own custom foods, ordered by name (case-insensitive). Never includes shared foods or another user's.

Replaces the name, the base unit and the per-100 nutrition of one of the caller's own custom foods. baseUnitType is Gram or Milliliter; left out, the food keeps its unit. Switching it also moves the items already logged for the food to the new unit (350 g becomes 350 ml), keeping their nutrition. 404 when the id does not exist, is a shared food or belongs to another user (the three look the same). Meals already logged keep the values they were saved with.

query.description: The caller's UTC offset in minutes (e.g. -180 for Brasilia). Days are grouped by the caller's own calendar day instead of UTC. Optional, defaults to 0.

request.description: Each item is a quantity and a unit. unit: Gram|Kilogram for a food, Milliliter|Liter for a drink (the food's baseUnitType says which); the other kind is a 400. mealType: Breakfast|Lunch|Dinner|Snack. Nutrition is computed and snapshotted server-side -- do not send calories/protein/carbs/fat. LoggedAt is set to the current server time and returned in the response; there is no date field on create.

A meal can mix catalog items (foodId) and AI-estimated items (estimatedFood, sent back exactly as an estimate returned it); each item has exactly one of the two. Every estimated item's captureId must be one of the meal's captures, and a capture with hasPhoto must have its photo uploaded (400 otherwise). On update, omitting captures keeps the meal's current ones; sending a list replaces them and deletes the photos of the captures left out. Each capture in the response carries a short-lived photoUrl.
Full replace, same shape as Create Meal (no date field here either). Items not included here are removed from the meal. LoggedAt is preserved from the original meal, not reset to the edit time.

item.name: Meal Estimates
item.description: AI estimates of a meal from a photo, a description, or both (docs/specs/meal-ai-estimate.md). Only users on the MealEstimates:AllowedUserIds allowlist may call these (403 MealEstimateAccessDenied otherwise; GET /profile reports it as canEstimateMeals), and each user gets 20 calls an hour across both routes (429 TooManyRequests). Estimates are also capped at 300 a month across every user (429 MonthlyEstimateLimitReached, until the next UTC month). Nothing is saved here: send the returned items to Create Meal.

request.description: Returns a captureId and a presigned S3 URL valid for 5 minutes, plus the headers the upload must send exactly. The test script stores captureId and photoUploadUrl in collection variables for the next requests.

PUT the JPEG straight to S3 (pick the file in the Body tab). No bearer token: the URL is already signed, and an Authorization header would make S3 reject it. Photos above 5 MB are refused when estimated.

Photo estimate: captureId from the upload slot, description optional (up to 500 characters). When the description contradicts the photo, the description wins. 400 if the photo is missing, expired or too large; 422 NoFoodRecognized; 502 EstimateUnavailable when the model fails. Send it again with another description on the same captureId to re-estimate.

Description-only estimate: no captureId, description of 10 to 500 characters. The response carries a new captureId (hasPhoto false) to send as the meal's capture; the test script stores it in captureId.

query.description: The caller's UTC offset in minutes (e.g. -180 for Brasilia). Days are grouped by the caller's own calendar day instead of UTC. Optional, defaults to 0.

request.description: Aggregates meals, water entries and weight entries into one payload for charting. Returns 404 until the caller has upserted a profile at least once (Upsert Profile). currentWeightKilograms is the most recent weight entry the user has ever logged, regardless of from/to -- it answers "what do I weigh right now", not "what did I weigh in this window". weightHistory only contains days with an actual entry (sparse, since weight is not expected to be logged daily); nutritionHistory has exactly one entry per calendar day in [from, to], zero-filled for days with no meals or water logged, so charts render a continuous line without gap-filling client-side.

variable.description: Set by Create Photo Upload Slot and Estimate Meal from Description.
Set by Create Photo Upload Slot; expires 5 minutes after it is created.
